name: Gauge theory transforms four-manifold topology
summary: Solutions of the Yang-Mills and later Seiberg-Witten equations give invariants distinguishing smooth structures on four-manifolds, results unreachable by classical topology.

name: Perelman's proof of the Poincare conjecture
summary: Ricci flow with surgery, controlled by an entropy functional and Alexandrov-space compactness, classifies three-manifolds and gives the Poincare and geometrisation conjectures.

name: Wavelets
summary: Multiresolution ideas from signal processing and quantum field theory are merged with harmonic analysis to give orthonormal bases of compactly supported functions.

name: Supersymmetry and Morse theory
summary: Supersymmetric quantum mechanics gives an analytic proof of the Morse inequalities, a template for later physics-inspired invariants.

name: Quantum computation: Shor's algorithm
summary: A quantum Fourier transform finds periods and hence factors integers in polynomial time, tying quantum mechanics to complexity and cryptography.

name: Teichmuller dynamics: homogeneous dynamics on moduli spaces
summary: Ratner-style measure rigidity is adapted to the SL(2,R) action on moduli of abelian differentials, proving the magic wand theorem.

name: Geometric Langlands and its physics
summary: The arithmetic correspondence is reformulated for curves over the complex numbers with sheaves in place of functions, and electric-magnetic duality in gauge theory is identified as its physical origin.

name: Faltings: Mordell's conjecture via moduli and heights
summary: Finiteness of rational points on curves of genus at least 2 is proved by combining the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties, moduli of abelian varieties and height theory.

name: Contact topology and the h-principle (Eliashberg)
summary: Overtwisted contact structures are classified by homotopy theory, separating flexible from rigid phenomena.

name: Unipotent flows and the Oppenheim conjecture
summary: Values of indefinite quadratic forms at integer points are controlled by showing orbits of unipotent subgroups on homogeneous spaces are well-behaved.
